column1: # The checks CI makes of each game run (ci/runs.tsv), evaluated by ci/check-log.py.
# side: the run's side. runs: the runs it is checked in, any of: * (every run of the side with the test mods), extra (one
#   with other mods too), run ids; !<run> leaves one out. gate: yes for a check that fails its run where the run's
#   gates admit it (ci/runs.tsv), no for one that is only reported.
# Platform columns: where it applies (ci/plan.py), the reasons for where it doesn't in why_not.
# file: what it reads, relative to the run: out (the console), log (the game log, or the console without one), report
#   (fabric-bridge-report.txt), report#<section> (a section of it), debug (debug.log), crash (crash reports), status
#   (the server's start, or the client's exit status), failures (mixin-failures.json), warm and warm-report (the
#   console and the report of a second launch), mods (the mods folder's listing), linkage (ci/forge-shared/standin-linkage.py's output); several,
# pattern: a regular expression a line must match; !<pattern> one no line may match; #<n> <pattern> exactly n lines,
#   #<n>+ at least n; <file,...> before it reads other files; conditions join with && and ||, && binding first.
#   {minecraft}, {platform} and {loader} are the run's. A missing "<check> OK" line with "<check> SKIPPED: <why>" in
#   its place is a SKIP: another mod's module answers that check.
# when: a condition (the same form) that must hold for the check to apply, else it is a SKIP with its "when:" reason.
# same: rows that are the same check on another platform (their test mods log FABRICATED-TEST on NeoForge and
#   FABRICATED-FORGE-TEST on Forge until they are one suite) share it.
